# AWS Service Quotas

Read informational built-in quotas and store quota increase requests without enforcing limits.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `servicequotas` |
| Signing name | `servicequotas` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2019-06-24` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records only |
| Selected operations | 9 of 26 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-service-quotas) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Quota values are informational and never enforced by TinyStack; defaults are a small static snapshot, not live AWS account limits.
- No approvals or support cases: requests remain PENDING and applied values never change.
- No resource-level quota contexts, applied/requested level filters, SupportCaseAllowed, templates, automatic management, tags, usage metrics or quota associations.
- IAM and S3 quotas are marked global but request records are isolated by account and Region; global quotas are readable in every Region.
- Request history is retained indefinitely rather than limited to the AWS 90-day window; requests have no delete operation.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
